name: the harness layer: plain-English intent -> validated block sequence
status: PROPOSED - not locked, nothing built yet

roles.who_reads_english: the harness model (Claude or Gemini), as in the talk chain User -> Harness -> Mule -> Godot. The mule never sees English.
roles.what_we_build: the deterministic side, so that a misreading by the harness cannot reach the project: a capability card, a compact plan format, a full dry run on a throwaway copy, one-call execution and an undo
roles.files: one new file, cascade_plan.py, plus cascade_vocab.json. The clock is not patched: the plan tool imports it, like the sweep does.

flow: 2. the harness restates the goal in one sentence and waits for a yes (the harness rule you already use)
3. the harness works from the catalog (python3 cascade_plan.py catalog, pasted into the session) and writes a compact plan with its assumptions stated
4. cascade_plan.py dry-run plan.json: the whole pipeline on a temporary copy, no mule, nothing real touched
5. the harness shows the plan and the dry-run verdict; the user says go
6. cascade_plan.py run plan.json: the real chain, one model load, tagged with the plan id
7. report; cascade_plan.py undo <plan id> if the user wants it back

compact_plan.expansion: the tool expands each step into primitive blocks: when = add_method + connect_signal (handler named _on_<node>_<signal>); the type comes from the registry, and time_slot, subnet, ref, exclude and frame ids are filled in. The harness supplies only the essentials, so it cannot get a type or an address wrong.

prints: hosts: name, class, script, registered properties with types
signals the harness may use (no arguments), each with how it fires: by itself on entering the tree, by itself on leaving it, or never by itself (the probe emits it)
signals that are out of reach and why (they carry arguments)
existing handlers, with what each one does (pass, print, assignment, or hand-written) and which signal each is connected to
the step menu above with its limits
catalog.size: a screen or two, so it fits in a session

vocabulary.rule: when two signals fit (ready vs tree_entered) the harness picks one, says so under assumptions and lets the user override

supported_intents: add a function that sets a property / prints / does nothing

refusal_boundary.rule: an intent outside the list is refused in plain words with the nearest supported plan, never guessed at
refused: several actions in one handler (multi-statement bodies are an open slot)
expressions and relative changes: double the speed, add 10
handlers with arguments, and signals that carry arguments
another node, spawning or instancing scenes, timers, input
a property, signal or node that is not in the catalog
changing an existing handler's body (editing is an open slot)

dry_run.how: copy the whole workspace to a temporary folder; run every block through the real clock in rehearsal mode, with the canonical answer standing in for the mule (the exact statement the harness would write); real GI-1, GI-3, Godot parse check, apply, reload check, behavior check (Slot 5) and registry refresh, all on the copy
dry_run.what_it_proves: everything except what the mule itself will type, and that part is guarded by GI-3
dry_run.report: per block: status, verify verdict, the guard's own message when refused; then READY, NOOP or REFUSED

run_and_undo.run: python3 cascade_plan.py run plan.json: dry run first (a failure stops here), then the real chain in one process with the plan id as run id; saves plans/<id>/plan.json, the blocks and result.json (statuses, backups, file hashes after)
run_and_undo.undo: python3 cascade_plan.py undo <id>: restore the plan's backups in reverse order, rebuild the registry
run_and_undo.safety: undo refuses when a file changed after the plan (a later plan touched it) and names the plans to undo first, so it can never wipe newer work
run_and_undo.status: python3 cascade_plan.py status lists plans, their intent and whether they were undone

tested_on_godot_4_3.preflight_by_parse_check: planned function + connect statement on a temporary copy of the script: exit 0; the connect statement without the function (order mistake) exit 1; a typo exit 1; the real script untouched
tested_on_godot_4_3.dry_run: a two-block plan on a temporary copy: add_method APPLIED/verify PASS, connect_signal APPLIED/verify PASS in 12 s; the same plan plus a third block with a mistyped signal: block 3 refused by the real guard (GI_1 signal 'tree_entred' is not a signal of %Player); the real project's hashes identical before and after
tested_on_godot_4_3.undo: two applied blocks restored from the ledger's backups in reverse order: all three file hashes identical to before; the rebuilt registry no longer lists the new handler

decisions_to_lock: 1. the compact plan format; the tool expands it and fills every field the registry knows
2. the catalog and the editable vocabulary, with the supported-intent list and the refusal boundary
3. dry-run = the real pipeline on a throwaway copy with canonical answers; no mule, no writes
4. run (chain with a plan id and saved results) and undo with the newer-plans-first safety rule, plus status
5. the harness protocol: restate the goal and wait for yes, state assumptions, refuse outside the boundary, dry-run before any real run
